expected_burke_pentad_candidate: Agency (anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 — provenance: anticipatory-projection). The dimension's whole expository thrust is structurally aligned with Burke's Agency pentad-term (capability + means of action), making this the cleanest pentad mapping in the volume — but Burke is wholly absent from Calleja's text and references (cite_check: 0 hits), so the mapping is dissertation-side projection only.
expected_uexkull_anchor_candidate: Funktionskreis (anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 — provenance: anticipatory-projection). Calleja's player<->avatar feedback loop (key-press -> avatar response -> perceptual feedback -> next key-press), especially in the Morris-cited 'think with their fingers' passage and the Bladerunner 'Quan' quote, structurally parallels Uexküll's perception-action functional cycle (Merkmal -> Merkorgan -> Innenwelt -> Wirkorgan -> Wirkmal). Calleja has zero Uexküll-vocabulary and the Gibson-via-affordance mediation hypothesis is FALSIFIED per Phase 0 cite-check — Calleja uses 'affordance' once in this chapter (line 2383, on Mirror's Edge) generically and without Gibson attribution.
expected_ontological_grounding_candidate: aisthesis-kinesis via Bowin AMT + Phantasia Cluster (anticipatory projection — provenance: anticipatory-projection). The continuity-of-motion analysis underlying kinesthetic pleasure (Sunniva's 'continuous motion' surfing simile, Bladerunner's 'Quan' as unmediated willed action, Mirror's Edge as 'a game about creating a continuity of movement') is the canonical Bowin Aristotelian-Motion-and-Time bridge target. The 'disposition to act' / anticipatory-readiness theme (Red Orchestra sniper) bridges to Heidegger BCAP analyses of kairotic readiness. Calleja cites no Aristotle, no Heidegger SZ-era work, and no Merleau-Ponty.

notes: CHAPTER STRUCTURE (verified): five named subsections — 'Macro Phase: Agency', 'Micro Phase: In-Game Control', 'Modes of Control in Game Environments', 'Modes of Game Control', 'Kinesthetic Pleasure'. The latter three are nested under the Micro Phase. Manifest seed listed only the Macro Phase heading; this Phase 1 pass adds the four additional headings. SURPRISES: (1) Manifest interlocutor list ('Murray, Schott') is incomplete — actual chapter engages SEVEN interlocutors (Murray, Schott, Mateas+Stern, Giddens, Malaby, Morris, Swalwell+Van Rooyen-McLeay). Mateas+Stern's local/global agency distinction and Giddens's capability-not-intention reframing are substantively load-bearing for Calleja's preferred (Giddens-inflected) agency definition. (2) Calleja's symbolic/mimetic/symbiotic control TRICHOTOMY is far more developed than the manifest's 'control schemes' concept-seed suggested, and Figure 4.3 ('Forms of control in digital games') visualizes this continuum — it is a load-bearing typology candidate for Phase 2. (3) The Sunniva quote uses the word 'flow' (line 2325) but is participant-vernacular, NOT Csikszentmihalyi-cited — confirms Phase 0 finding of zero Csikszentmihalyi engagement. (4) The Mirror's Edge passage uses 'affordances' (line 2383) once, generically — confirms Phase 0 Gibson-falsification (zero Gibson attribution despite affordance-talk). (5) Bladerunner's 'Quan' (an idiom for unmediated willed action drawn from the film 'Jerry Maguire') is a participant-coined construct Calleja preserves as a vernacular name for internalized control — Phase 2 should NOT promote it to canonical concept, but should track it as a vivid participant-vocabulary illustration of internalization. (6) BRENDA LAUREL listed in Phase 0 §5 census as Ch.4 interlocutor on agency — NOT detected in the Ch.4 fulltext sweep; Phase 2 should re-verify (may be a Phase 0 misattribution; Laurel likely belongs to Ch.2 immersion-via-theater discussion). (7) The chapter ends without a formal 'Conclusion' subheading; closure is an unnamed two-paragraph coda (lines 2442-2462) tying kinesthetic involvement to other PIM dimensions and emphasizing movement as foundational to other forms of involvement.
